repo.description:
### Summary

OAuth access tokens are signed with the same secret as first-party session tokens, so the session
strategy accepted an OAuth bearer token as a full interactive session.

### Details

Access tokens issued by the OAuth token service were signed with the instance's JWT secret. The session strategy validated any such token and returned the associated user, so a token issued for a narrow OAuth scope authenticated its holder on first-party endpoints as though it were a browser session. In the Enterprise build, the exchange in `short-lived-token.strategy.ts` that turns a single sign-on token into a session also accepted an OAuth access token and issued a full session with a refresh token, and the socket handshake in `NocoSocket.ts` accepted the same token. The session strategy, the exchange and the socket handshake now refuse OAuth access tokens, and the exchange accepts only tokens minted for single sign-on.

### Impact

A token obtained for a limited OAuth scope could be used against first-party APIs with the full
privileges of the granting user, bypassing the scope restrictions the consent flow presented.

### Credit

This issue was reported by [@hash3liZer](https://github.com/hash3liZer),
[@XlabAITeam](https://github.com/XlabAITeam), [@keenanwgn](https://github.com/keenanwgn),
[@liangjs](https://github.com/liangjs), [@A7um](https://github.com/A7um), and
[@eros938](https://github.com/eros938).
repo.summary: OAuth Access Token Accepted as First-Party Session
